lesson: Comparing weights through strips and spectral tails

figures.title: A positive test in the core recovers every weight value
figures.caption: For an L2-normalized compactly supported f, the positive lift X_x = pi(x^(1/2)) lambda(f)* lambda(f) pi(x^(1/2)) satisfies T(X_x) = pi(x). Consequently the dual weights evaluate X_x as the original weights evaluate x, so dualization reflects order on the entire positive cone, including infinite values. The arrows display exact identities, not a finite-dimensional model.
figures.alt: Diagram from an arbitrary positive x in M to its positive lift X_x in the continuous core and then, through T, to pi(x). The equality of original and dual evaluations proves order reflection.
figures.assumptions: An arbitrary von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal semifinite reference weight; its continuous core, the normalized averaging operator-valued weight, and normal weights eta and nu. The concluding inequality assumes dual eta is at most dual nu.

figures.title: Half-depth order does not force depth-one order
figures.caption: For h = diag(1,2) and k = [[2,1],[1,3]], k-h is positive, so the associated trace weights compare at depth one-half. At depth one, xi = (5,-4) gives <(k^2-h^2)xi,xi> = -4. The forced endpoint hk^(-1) sends (6,-7) to (5,-8), increasing squared norm from 85 to 89. The dashed circle has exact radius sqrt(85); no maximal-strip claim is made.
figures.alt: Two exact matrix tests and a coordinate plot showing hk inverse sends a vector on the radius square-root-85 circle to a vector outside it with squared norm 89.
figures.assumptions: The specified positive invertible two-by-two matrices and the usual trace on M2(C). The vector picture uses their invariant real coordinate plane.

figures.title: The lower half-plane selects nonpositive frequencies
figures.caption: With Fourier convention hat f(p) = integral f(t) exp(itp) dt, a scalar mode exp(itp) has modulus exp(yp) at t-iy. The Poisson kernels have mass one and produce a bounded lower-half-plane extension for nonpositive spectral support. The sampled p=-1 mode decays with depth, p=0 remains constant, and p=1 grows. For phi = exp(-1) psi the balanced matrix units e12 and e21 therefore have frequencies -1 and +1 respectively.
figures.alt: Three panels show positive Poisson kernels, decay of a negative-frequency scalar mode down the complex lower half-plane, and scalar magnitudes for frequencies minus one, zero and plus one.
figures.assumptions: The general statement uses a point-ultraweakly continuous automorphism group on a von Neumann algebra and an element with spectrum in (-infinity,0]. Curves and shading are numerical samples of displayed exact scalar formulas; the balanced example uses faithful normal semifinite weights with scalar ratio exp(-1).
figures.kind: exact formulas with labeled numerical samples
